findings.title: No check grades a strip footing's width against its soil bearing: the x=18' centreline strips (20" wide) carry 3,205 plf D+L by the house's own basis note, 1,923 psf against the sheet's 1,500 psf
files: packages/engine/src/typehaus/checks/structural/bearing_wall_footing.py:1-30 (grades projection P and bearing points only)
houses/catlin/plan/assemblies/footings.py:131 (source cites 'IRC Table R403.1', no check reads it)

evidence.measured: Model: FT-B-CS/CS2/CN/CN2 are 20.00" x 8.00" plain strips (solids z -117.44..-109.44, bbox x 206..226). main_floor_truss_basis.md s5 totals the x=18' wall at 1,225 plf D + 1,980 plf L + 630 plf S = 3,205 plf D+L (2,610 at 0.75 L+S). 3,205 plf / (20/12 ft) = 1,923 psf; adding the strip's own weight (20x8x150 pcf = 167 plf) 2,023 psf. S-001 prints SOIL BEARING 1500.0 psf; required width at 1,500 psf = 3,205/1,500 = 25.6" before self-weight. The note's footing paragraph only says the 12" pour 'weighed 1,200 plf' and that bearing_wall_footing passes, which grades geometry. Engineering register (engineering.json, 51 items) has no strip-footing item; the only engine width table is R403.4 for crushed stone (crushed_stone_footings.py:61).
evidence.expected: A concrete strip under a three-storey bearing line is sized against the soil value either by IRC Table R403.1(1) (not encoded anywhere in the engine) or by a stated bearing calc; either way a number on the sheet. Hand arithmetic from the house's own loads should land at or under 1,500 psf, or the strip is wider than 20".
